recommendations.title: Mexican Gothic
recommendations.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
recommendations.reason: Their love of atmospheric horror with literary depth (Our Wives Under the Sea, The Haunting of Hill House, Dark Matter by Paver) and their interest in historical fiction makes this lush Gothic horror set in 1950s Mexico a natural fit.

recommendations.title: Plain Bad Heroines
recommendations.author: Emily M. Danforth
recommendations.reason: Their taste for literary horror with Gothic atmosphere (The Last House on Needless Street, Summer Sons, The September House) and LGBTQ+ themes (What Moves the Dead, Tipping the Velvet) makes this dual-timeline sapphic horror novel an excellent match.

recommendations.title: The Wanting Seed
recommendations.author: Anthony Burgess
recommendations.reason: Their appetite for dark dystopian classics (1984, Brave New World, Concrete Island) and speculative fiction exploring social collapse (The Deluge, Parable of the Talents) makes this bleak Malthusian satire a compelling fit.

recommendations.title: A Gentleman in Moscow
recommendations.author: Amor Towles
recommendations.reason: Their enjoyment of richly character-driven literary fiction spanning decades (The Thousand Autumns of Jacob de Zoet, The Books of Jacob, Lessons) suggests this absorbing novel of a Russian count under house arrest in a luxury hotel would deeply satisfy.

recommendations.title: The Grip of It
recommendations.author: Jac Jemc
recommendations.reason: Their strong pull toward literary haunted-house horror (The Haunting of Hill House, House of Leaves, We Used to Live Here) and experimental fiction makes this psychologically unsettling novel about a couple consumed by a malevolent house a natural next read.

recommendations.title: The Raw Shark Texts
recommendations.author: Steven Hall
recommendations.reason: Their enthusiasm for formally inventive, mind-bending fiction (House of Leaves, Piranesi, How to Live Safely in a Science Fictional Universe) and genre-blurring narratives makes this postmodern thriller about a man hunted by a conceptual shark an ideal choice.

recommendations.title: The Dispossessed
recommendations.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
recommendations.reason: Their interest in philosophically rich science fiction that interrogates social systems (Parable of the Talents, Chain-Gang All-Stars, The Deluge) makes this landmark dual-world novel contrasting anarchism and capitalism a compelling and natural fit.

recommendations.title: Trust Exercise
recommendations.author: Susan Choi
recommendations.reason: Their appetite for formally inventive literary fiction that subverts narrative expectations (The Raw Shark Texts, No One Is Talking About This, Piranesi) and their interest in coming-of-age stories with dark undertones (Never Let Me Go, My Dark Vanessa) makes this layered, reality-questioning novel a strong match.

recommendations.author: Kate Summerscale
recommendations.reason: Their interest in gothic horror, psychological fiction, and nonfiction crime/history (as seen with House of Leaves, The Haunting of Hill House already read, and The Terror on their list) suggests they'd love this true account of a 1930s haunting investigated with real historical and psychological depth.

recommendations.title: Mexican Gothic
recommendations.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
recommendations.reason: Given their enthusiasm for Silver Nitrate (already read) and their want-to-read list full of gothic horror like The September House, Dark Matter, and Our Wives Under the Sea, this lush horror novel set in 1950s Mexico would be a perfect fit.

recommendations.title: The Drowning Kind
recommendations.author: Jennifer McMahon
recommendations.reason: Their want-to-read list is heavy with atmospheric, literary horror (The Lamplighters, Solace House, Old Country) and they've read The Haunting of Hill House and Rebecca, making this eerie, dual-timeline supernatural thriller a natural next read.

recommendations.title: The Actual Star
recommendations.author: Monica Byrne
recommendations.reason: Their interest in ambitious, multi-stranded speculative fiction spanning history and futurity — as evidenced by Cloud Cuckoo Land, The Bone Clocks already read, and Little, Big on their list — aligns perfectly with this sweeping, literary science fantasy epic.

recommendations.title: All the White Spaces
recommendations.author: Ally Wilkes
recommendations.reason: Their want-to-read list includes The Terror and The Lamplighters, and they've already read The Wager, pointing to a clear love of isolated, historical, atmospheric horror — this Antarctic gothic about a queer stowaway on a doomed expedition hits all those notes.

recommendations.title: The Ruin of Kings
recommendations.author: Jenn Lyons
recommendations.reason: Their want-to-read list features complex epic fantasy like The Way of Kings, Gardens of the Moon, and The Farseer Trilogy, and they've read Mistborn and A Game of Thrones, making this intricate, multi-layered fantasy with unreliable narrators an obvious fit.

recommendations.title: Small Rain
recommendations.author: Garth Greenwell
recommendations.reason: Their want-to-read list includes literary fiction with emotional and philosophical weight — Foster, Filthy Animals, Luster, Beautiful World Where Are You — and Greenwell's quiet, profound novel about illness and intimacy fits squarely in that literary-fiction vein they clearly love.

recommendations.author: Jack Kerouac

recommendations.title: The Raw Shark Texts
recommendations.author: Steven Hall
recommendations.reason: Their fondness for genre-bending, conceptually adventurous fiction—evidenced by 'House of Leaves,' 'How to Live Safely in a Science Fictional Universe,' and 'Little, Big'—makes this postmodern thriller about memory and identity a strong match.

recommendations.title: Butcher's Crossing
recommendations.author: John Williams
recommendations.reason: Their interest in 'Augustus' by John Williams and gritty American literary fiction from authors like Larry Brown and Cormac McCarthy makes this stark, existential Western a natural fit.

recommendations.title: The Little Stranger
recommendations.author: Sarah Waters
recommendations.reason: Their love of Sarah Waters via 'Tipping the Velvet' and 'Fingersmith,' combined with their appetite for slow-burn literary horror like 'We Have Always Lived in the Castle' and 'The Terror,' makes this haunted-house novel a perfect fit.

recommendations.title: The Moor's Account
recommendations.author: Laila Lalami
recommendations.reason: Their interest in historical fiction with rich cultural scope—evidenced by 'The Books of Jacob,' 'The Thousand Autumns of Jacob de Zoet,' and 'Undaunted Courage'—makes this Booker-longlisted novel about the first African explorer of America a compelling choice.

recommendations.title: Galveston
recommendations.author: Nic Pizzolatto
recommendations.reason: Their fondness for noir-inflected Southern literary fiction—seen through 'Bluebird, Bluebird,' 'Cottonmouths,' and 'Joe'—makes this dark, atmospheric crime novel about fate and redemption along the Gulf Coast an excellent match.

recommendations.title: Mexican Gothic
recommendations.author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
recommendations.reason: Given their interest in Silver Nitrate by Moreno-Garcia and atmospheric horror titles like The September House and The Terror, this lush gothic horror set in 1950s Mexico should resonate deeply.

recommendations.title: Plain Bad Heroines
recommendations.author: Emily M. Danforth
recommendations.reason: Their taste for layered literary horror with queer themes, as seen with Our Wives Under the Sea, Summer Sons, and What Moves the Dead, aligns perfectly with this dual-timeline gothic novel.

recommendations.title: The Night Country
recommendations.author: Melissa Albert
recommendations.reason: Their fondness for dark fairy-tale fantasy like Fairy Tale by Stephen King, The Night Circus, and Starling House points directly to this sharp, atmospheric YA dark fantasy follow-up.

recommendations.title: The Trees
recommendations.author: Ali Shaw
recommendations.reason: Their love of literary ecological fiction and fantasy such as The Vaster Wilds, The Overstory, and Blue Skies makes this haunting novel about England swallowed overnight by a primeval forest an excellent fit.

recommendations.title: Leave the Gun, Take the Cannoli
recommendations.author: Mark Seal
recommendations.reason: Their nonfiction interests spanning true crime, cultural history, and narrative nonfiction like Rogues by Patrick Radden Keefe and Dark Wire make this behind-the-scenes history of The Godfather a compelling pick.

recommendations.title: The Devil in Silver
recommendations.author: Victor LaValle
recommendations.reason: Their appreciation for Lone Women by LaValle and horror titles with literary ambition like The Only Good Indians and Our Share of Night makes this darkly comic institutional horror novel a strong fit.

recommendations.title: The Mercies
recommendations.author: Kiran Millwood Hargrave
recommendations.reason: Their interest in historical fiction with dark atmospheres, queer themes, and literary depth as seen with Fingersmith, Woman of Light, and The Terror points toward this haunting novel about witchcraft trials in 17th-century Norway.
